mainTopic: Managing property of minors and captives, and רב חסדא's ruling against a violent heir
overview: The גמרא finishes the rule that a relative who manages a קטן's land never gains a חזקה, even after the קטן grows up. It suggests three limits to the rule אין מורידין קרוב לנכסי קטן, and then rejects all of them. Next comes a case: an old woman and one daughter were taken captive, and another daughter died and left a small child. אביי shows that neither the free sister nor the child can simply manage the property. He splits it, giving half to the sister and putting a steward over the other half. רבא says one steward should manage it all. When news comes that the grandmother died, they disagree the same way about the captive daughter's third. Finally, רב חסדא judges a man who claims to be the brother of the powerful מרי בר איסק. He puts the burden of proof on מרי, because frightened witnesses may stay silent but will not lie. Once the brother is confirmed, he shares even in the orchards מרי planted.

steps.title: Even after the minor grows up
steps.stepSummary: A relative who held a קטן's property does not gain a חזקה, even if he kept holding it after the קטן grew up.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even if he grew up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a ruling from just before: a relative who held a קטן's land gets no חזקה, and this is true even after the קטן becomes an adult.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally three years of holding land without protest creates a חזקה. Here it does not, even after the קטן grows up. The reason given is that the young owner may not know the land is really his, so his silence proves nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: he grew up, became an adult
a claim of ownership based on holding the land over time

phrases.english: And even if he grew up.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ruling from the earlier part of the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A relative's holding of a קטן's land never gives him a חזקה, even after the קטן grows up.

steps.title: Three suggested limits to the rule
steps.stepSummary: The rule against putting a relative in charge might apply only to the קטן's brothers from the father's side, only to fields, and only where no division document was written.
steps.simpleTranslation: We only said this about brothers from the father's side, but brothers from the mother's side are no problem. And even with brothers from the father's side, we only said it about fields, but houses are no problem. And even with fields, we only said it when no division document was made. But if a division document was made, it is publicly known.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests three ways to narrow the rule that אין מורידין קרוב לנכסי קטן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry is that the relative might later claim the property is his. Brothers on the mother's side are not heirs to the father's land, so their claim would not be believed. With houses, the neighbors know who owns what. If the father wrote a division document, everyone knows which share is whose.

keyTerms.meaning: brothers from the father's side (who are heirs)
brothers from the mother's side (who are not heirs)
a document that divides the property

steps.confusionAlert: Do not hold on to these limits. The very next step throws all three out.

phrases.english: And we only said this about brothers from the father's side,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל בְּאַחֵי דְאִמָּא לֵית לַן בַּהּ.
phrases.english: but with brothers from the mother's side, we have no problem with it.

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲחֵי דְאַבָּא נָמֵי לָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא בְּאַרְעָתָא,
phrases.english: And even with brothers from the father's side, we only said it about fields,
but with houses, we have no problem with it.
And even with fields, we only said it
when he did not make a division document,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל עֲבִיד עִיטְדָּא – קָלָא אִית לַהּ.
phrases.english: but if he made a division document, it becomes publicly known.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Suggests limits to the rule just stated.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Suggested view: the rule applies only to brothers from the father's side, only to fields, and only when there is no division document.

steps.title: No limits: never put a relative in charge
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects all three limits. A relative is never put in charge of a קטן's property.
steps.simpleTranslation: But that is not so. It makes no difference whether they are brothers from the father's side or from the mother's side, fields or houses, or whether a division document was made or not. We do not put a relative in charge.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects every limit from the last step and keeps the rule completely general.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The three reasons for leniency are all set aside. The worry that a relative may come to treat the property as his own applies in every case. So אין מורידין applies with no exceptions.

keyTerms.meaning: but it is not so (a rejection)
we put someone in charge (of property)

steps.whatToRemember: The final rule: any relative, any type of property, with or without a division document. We never put a relative in charge of a קטן's property.

phrases.english: But that is not so.

phrases.aramaic: לָא שְׁנָא אַחֵי דְאַבָּא וְלָא שְׁנָא אַחֵי דְאִמָּא,
phrases.english: It makes no difference whether they are brothers from the father's side or brothers from the mother's side,

phrases.aramaic: לָא שְׁנָא אַרְעָתָא וְלָא שְׁנָא בָּתֵּי,
phrases.english: no difference between fields and houses,

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא שְׁנָא עֲבִיד עִיטְדָּא לָא שְׁנָא לָא עֲבִיד עִיטְדָּא –
phrases.english: and no difference whether he made a division document or did not,
we do not put a relative in charge.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the limits suggested in step 2.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The concern about a relative applies everywhere, so none of the differences matter.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: We never put a relative in charge of a קטן's property.

steps.title: The captive grandmother story
steps.stepSummary: An old woman with three daughters was captured with one daughter. Of the other two daughters, one died and left a small child.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was an old woman who had three daughters. She and one daughter were taken captive. Of the other two daughters, one died and left a small child.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up a real case. This prepares for אביי's question about who should manage the old woman's property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two possible managers are left: the surviving daughter, who is free, and the dead daughter's small child. Each one connects to a different rule about putting someone in charge of property.

phrases.aramaic: הָהִיא סָבְתָּא דַּהֲוַיָא לַהּ תְּלָת בְּנָתָא.
phrases.english: There was a certain old woman who had three daughters.
She and one daughter were taken captive.
Of the other two daughters,
one of them died and left a small child.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהִיא סָבְתָּא דַּהֲוַיָא לַהּ תְּלָת בְּנָתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new case that uses the rule just settled.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The facts: the grandmother and one daughter are captive, one daughter is free, and one daughter died and left a small child.

steps.title: אביי asks what to do
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks who should be put in charge of the captive grandmother's property.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: What should we do?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי asks the question. This sets up the two options that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The property needs a manager while its owner is in captivity. The question is which of the two remaining family members may take charge.

phrases.english: אביי said: What should we do?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the case just described.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who should manage the captive grandmother's property?

steps.title: Option one: give it to the surviving sister
steps.stepSummary: The surviving sister cannot be put in charge. Maybe the grandmother died, and then part of the property belongs to the child, and a relative cannot manage a קטן's property.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us put the property in the hands of the sister. But maybe the old woman died, and we do not put a relative in charge of a child's property!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי tries the first option, the free sister, and points out its problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the grandmother already died, the dead daughter's child inherits a share. Then the sister would be a relative managing a קטן's property, which we just learned is never allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: we do not put a relative in charge of a child's property

phrases.english: Let us put the property in the hands of the sister.
phrases.notes: This means the free daughter, who is the small child's aunt.

phrases.english: But maybe the old woman died,
and we do not put a relative in charge of a child's property!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The first answer to אביי's question, which is then rejected.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: If the grandmother died, the child owns a share, and a relative may not manage a קטן's property.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the rule from step 3 being used in a real case.

steps.title: Option two: give it to the child
steps.stepSummary: The child cannot be put in charge either. Maybe the grandmother is still alive, and a קטן is not put in charge of a captive's property.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us put the property in the hands of the child. But maybe the old woman did not die, and we do not put a child in charge of a captive's property!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי tries the second option, the child, and finds that it fails too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the grandmother is alive, the property is still hers as a שבוי. A קטן is not put in charge of a captive's property. So both options are blocked. The next step gives אביי's solution.

keyTerms.meaning: we do not put a child in charge of a captive's property

phrases.english: Let us put the property in the hands of the child.
But maybe the old woman did not die,
and we do not put a child in charge of a captive's property!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The second answer to אביי's question, which is also rejected.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: If the grandmother is alive, a קטן may not manage a captive's property.
steps.whatToRemember: אביי is stuck between two rules: אין מורידין קרוב לנכסי קטן, and אין מורידין קטן לנכסי שבוי.

steps.title: אביי's solution: half to the sister, a steward for the other half
steps.stepSummary: אביי rules that the surviving sister receives half of the property, and a steward is appointed over the other half on the child's behalf.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Therefore, we give half to the sister, and for the other half we appoint a steward on behalf of the child.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers his own question by splitting the property into two halves. Each half is handled differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sister's half is safe for her either way. If the captives died, she inherits it. If they are alive, a relative may manage a captive's property. The other half might belong to the child, and a relative cannot manage a קטן's property, so an outside steward manages it for him.

keyTerms.meaning: A steward or guardian appointed to manage property

phrases.english: Abaye said: Therefore,
phrases.notes: "Therefore" points back to steps 6 and 7: neither the sister nor the child can simply be put in charge of everything.

phrases.english: half we give to the sister.
And the other half,
we appoint a steward for it on behalf of the child.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the problem from steps 6 and 7 by dividing the property.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who manages the captive grandmother's property (from step 5)?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The sister gets half. An outside steward manages the other half for the child.

steps.title: רבא: one steward for all of it
steps.stepSummary: רבא argues that once a steward is appointed for one half, he should manage the other half too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Since we appoint a steward for one half, we appoint him for the other half as well.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא disagrees with אביי's split. He says one steward should handle the whole property until we learn what happened to the captives.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key word is מגו ("since"). A steward is needed anyway for the child's possible half. So רבא says it makes sense to put the whole estate under that steward instead of handing half to the sister.

keyTerms.meaning: Since / once (since this is already done, do that too)

phrases.english: Rava said:
Since we appoint a steward for one half,
we appoint him as steward for the other half too.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: מִגּוֹ דְּמוֹקְמִינַן אַפּוֹטְרוֹפָּא לְפַלְגָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different ruling from אביי's.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One steward manages the entire property until the captives' fate is known.

steps.title: News that the grandmother died: אביי divides into thirds
steps.stepSummary: Word comes that the grandmother has died. אביי now gives a third to the sister and a third to the child. He splits the captive daughter's third between the sister and a steward for the child.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the end they heard that the grandmother died. אביי said: We give a third to the sister and a third to the child. Of the remaining third, we give a sixth to the sister, and for the other sixth we appoint a steward for the child.
steps.whatsHappening: The case changes: now we know the grandmother died, but the captive daughter's fate is still unknown. אביי divides the estate again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Three daughters means three shares. The sister takes her own third. The child takes his dead mother's third. The captive daughter's third is uncertain. Half of it goes to the sister, and half is managed by a steward in case the captive died and the child is an heir.

keyTerms.meaning: A sixth (literally a small coin worth a sixth)

steps.confusionAlert: The דנקא (sixth) is half of the captive daughter's third, not a sixth of something new. Third + third + sixth + sixth = the whole estate.

phrases.english: In the end they heard that the old woman had died.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: תִּילְתָּא יָהֲבִינַן לַהּ לַאֲחָתָא,
phrases.english: Abaye said: We give a third to the sister,
and we give a third to the child.
And the remaining third,
we give a sixth to the sister,
and the other sixth,
we appoint a steward for it on behalf of the child.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies אביי's approach to the new facts.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sister gets 1/3 + 1/6. Child gets 1/3. A steward manages the last 1/6 for the child.

steps.title: רבא again: one steward for both sixths
steps.stepSummary: רבא holds that since a steward manages one sixth, he should also manage the other sixth.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Since a steward is appointed for one sixth, we also appoint a steward for the other sixth.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא repeats his same logic for the new situation. The captive daughter's whole third stays under one steward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The disagreement is the same as before, just on a smaller scale. אביי splits the uncertain share. רבא keeps it all under one steward until the captive's fate is known.
steps.whatToRemember: In both stages, אביי splits the uncertain property between the sister and a steward. רבא uses מגו to put all of the uncertain property under one steward.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Since a steward is appointed for one sixth,
we also appoint a steward for the other sixth.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: מִגּוֹ דְּמוֹקֵים אַפּוֹטְרוֹפָּא לְדַנְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with אביי's ruling in step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The captive daughter's whole third is managed by one steward.

steps.title: A stranger claims to be מרי בר איסק's brother
steps.stepSummary: A man from בי חוזאי comes to מרי בר איסק, claims to be his brother, and asks for a share of the inheritance. מרי says he doesn't know him.
steps.simpleTranslation: מרי בר איסק had a brother come to him from בי חוזאי. He said to him: Divide the inheritance with me. מרי said: I don't know you.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new story about someone claiming a share of an estate. It sets up the case that רב חסדא will judge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man claims he is a brother and should get half of their father's estate. מרי does not admit it. So the question is who has to prove what.

keyTerms.meaning: A wealthy, powerful man in this story
Divide with me (give me my share)

phrases.english: Mari bar Isak —
a brother came to him from Bei Chozai.
He said to him: Divide with me.
He said to him: I don't know you.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָרִי בַּר אִיסַק אֲתָא לֵיהּ אַחָא מִבֵּי חוֹזָאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new story, still about inheritance and property rights.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Case setup: a claimed brother demands a share, and the heir denies knowing him.

steps.title: רב חסדא: brothers really can fail to recognize each other
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא tells the claimant that מרי's answer is reasonable. He proves it from יוסף, whose brothers did not recognize him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He came before רב חסדא, who said to him: He spoke well to you, as it says, 'יוסף recognized his brothers, but they did not recognize him.' This teaches that יוסף left without a full beard and came back with a full beard.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא brings a פסוק to show that מרי could honestly not recognize his brother.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יוסף left as a young man with no beard and returned grown, so his brothers did not know him. In the same way, a brother who left long ago may look like a stranger. So מרי's claim is not suspicious.

keyTerms.meaning: He is saying well / he is right
A full beard (literally the 'sealing' of the beard)

phrases.english: He came before Rav Chisda.
He said to him: He is speaking well to you,
as it says: 'Joseph recognized his brothers'
'but they did not recognize him' —
this teaches that he left without a full beard
and came back with a full beard.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up מרי's answer from step 12.
steps.raayaObject: That מרי's "I don't know you" is believable.
steps.raayaSupportSource: בראשית 42:8, about יוסף and his brothers.

steps.title: רב חסדא: bring witnesses that you are his brother
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא tells the claimant to bring witnesses proving he is the brother.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Go bring witnesses that you are his brother.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא puts the burden of proof on the man asking for the money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since מרי's denial is reasonable, the claimant is the one taking money from someone else. So he must prove his claim with witnesses.

phrases.english: He said to him: Go bring witnesses
that you are his brother.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the practical ruling from step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The claimant must prove he is the brother.

steps.title: The brother: my witnesses are too scared to testify
steps.stepSummary: The claimant says he has witnesses, but they are afraid of מרי because he is a violent, powerful man.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I have witnesses, but they are afraid of him, because he is a powerful man.
steps.whatsHappening: The claimant pushes back on רב חסדא's ruling. He has proof, but it is blocked by fear.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem is not missing evidence. The witnesses are being scared off by the other side. That makes it unfair to leave the whole burden on the claimant.

phrases.english: He said to him: I have witnesses,
but they are afraid of him,
because he is a violent man.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the burden of proof set in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's demand that the claimant bring witnesses.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The witnesses exist but will not come because they fear מרי, so the claimant cannot meet the burden.

steps.title: רב חסדא turns the burden onto מרי
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא now tells מרי to bring witnesses that the man is not his brother.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to מרי himself: You go bring witnesses that he is not your brother.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא responds to the fear problem by switching who has to bring proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the powerful side is scaring off witnesses, רב חסדא no longer makes the weak claimant prove his case. Now מרי must prove the man is not his brother.
steps.whatToRemember: At first the burden is on the claimant. Once he says the witnesses fear the violent heir, רב חסדא moves the burden to the heir.

phrases.english: He said to the other one himself:
phrases.notes: Now רב חסדא is speaking to מרי בר איסק, not to the claimant.

phrases.english: You go bring witnesses
that he is not your brother.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ לְדִידֵיהּ: זִיל אַנְתְּ אַיְיתִי סָהֲדֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the problem from step 15 by reversing the burden of proof.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The claimant must always bring proof.
steps.terutzMaskana: When the defendant's power keeps witnesses away, the defendant must bring proof.

steps.title: מרי protests: the claimant should bring proof
steps.stepSummary: מרי בר איסק challenges רב חסדא's ruling by citing the rule that whoever wants to take money from another must bring proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: מרי said to him: Is this the law? Whoever wants to take something from his fellow must bring the proof!
steps.whatsHappening: מרי בר איסק objects to רב חסדא's ruling from Step 16, which forced him to bring witnesses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The normal rule is that the person trying to take money away (here, the man from בי חוזאי) must prove his claim. רב חסדא flipped that and put the burden on מרי, the one holding the property. מרי says this goes against the basic rule.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who wants to take something away from another person

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'אֲמַר לֵיהּ' is מרי speaking to רב חסדא, not רב חסדא speaking. The speakers switch back and forth in each line of this section.

phrases.english: He said to him: Is this the law?!
The one who takes from his fellow must bring the proof.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of Step 16 that מרי must bring witnesses.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's ruling that the one holding the property must bring witnesses.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The standard rule puts the burden of proof on the claimant, not on the one in possession.

steps.title: רב חסדא: This is how I judge violent people
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא explains that for violent, powerful people like מרי, he places the burden of proof on them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said to him: This is how I judge you and all your violent friends.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers מרי's protest by explaining his special approach to violent people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The normal rule assumes witnesses can freely testify. When the holder is so powerful that witnesses are afraid to speak against him, רב חסדא shifts the burden onto him. This is an exception in how the rule is carried out, not a rejection of the rule itself.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a בית דין may adjust who must bring proof when one side's power keeps witnesses from speaking.

phrases.english: He said to him: This is how I judge you
and all of your violent fellows.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of Step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Exception based on the circumstances: the holder's violence frightens the witnesses.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The claimant must always bring proof.
steps.terutzMaskana: When the holder is a violent person whose power scares the witnesses, the burden can be placed on him.

steps.title: מרי: The witnesses still won't tell the truth
steps.stepSummary: מרי argues that switching the burden won't help, because the frightened witnesses will come and still not testify truthfully.
steps.simpleTranslation: מרי said to him: In the end, the witnesses will come and they won't testify (truthfully).
steps.whatsHappening: מרי pushes back again, saying רב חסדא's ruling won't get at the truth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the witnesses are scared of him, they will be scared no matter who calls them. They will show up and not say the truth, and may even testify in מרי's favor. So the new ruling seems useless.

phrases.english: He said to him: In the end,
the witnesses will come and not testify.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: סוֹף סוֹף אָתוּ סָהֲדִי וְלָא מַסְהֲדִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reasoning behind Step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's assumption that shifting the burden will bring out the truth.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Witnesses who fear מרי will stay quiet about the truth or lie regardless of which side calls them.

steps.title: Witnesses won't commit two wrongs
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא answers that witnesses may stay silent out of fear, but they will not go further and actually lie.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said to him: They won't do two wrongs.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא explains why his ruling works even with frightened witnesses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Staying quiet out of fear is one wrong. Coming to court and testifying falsely would be a second, worse wrong. Witnesses might do the first, but they won't do both, so when מרי has to bring them, they will not lie for him.

phrases.english: He said to him: They do not do two (wrongs).
phrases.notes: The two wrongs: hiding the truth, and then also lying in court.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of Step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Psychological assumption about how witnesses behave.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Frightened witnesses will lie in מרי's favor.
steps.terutzMaskana: Witnesses may stay silent out of fear, but they will not also give false testimony.

steps.title: The witnesses confirm he is the brother
steps.stepSummary: In the end, witnesses come and testify that the man from בי חוזאי really is מרי's brother.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the end, witnesses came and said that he is his brother.
steps.whatsHappening: The story moves forward: רב חסדא's approach worked, and the truth came out. This sets up the next request.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This proves רב חסדא right: once מרי had to bring witnesses, they would not lie, and they confirmed the man is his brother. Now the brother is entitled to inherit, which opens a new question about the estate.

phrases.english: In the end, witnesses came
(and testified) that he is his brother.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reports the outcome of the dispute over witnesses.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The claimant is confirmed as מרי's brother and an heir.

steps.title: The brother asks for a share of the new orchards
steps.stepSummary: The brother demands a share not only of the original estate but also of the orchards and gardens מרי planted.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Divide with me also from the orchards and gardens that you planted.
steps.whatsHappening: A new claim begins: the brother wants a share of the improvements מרי made to the estate.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מרי planted orchards and gardens on the family land while his brother was away. The question now is whether that added value belongs only to מרי, who did the work, or to both brothers.

phrases.english: He said to him: Divide for me also
phrases.notes: Now it's the brother speaking to מרי.

phrases.english: from the orchards and gardens that you planted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לִפְלוֹג לִי נָמֵי מִפַּרְדֵּיסֵי וּבוּסְתָּנִי דִּשְׁתַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the confirmation that he is an heir and raises a new claim about improvements.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The brother claims a share of improvements made to the estate.

steps.title: רב חסדא backs the brother from a משנה
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא tells מרי that his brother is right, citing a משנה that improvements made by older sons to an estate are shared with the younger sons.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said to him: He is right, as we learned in a משנה: If a man left older and younger sons, and the older ones improved the property, the improvements go to the shared pot.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא supports the brother's claim with a proof from a משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה teaches that when some heirs improve an estate that has not been divided yet, the gain belongs to all the heirs. מרי is like the older sons who worked the land. His absent brother is like the younger sons, so he gets a share of the orchards too.

keyTerms.meaning: He speaks well, he is right
To the middle, shared by everyone

steps.whatToRemember: רב חסדא made the violent holder bring witnesses, because frightened witnesses may stay silent but won't lie. Once the brother was confirmed, he shared even in the improvements, since improvements to an undivided estate go to all the heirs.
steps.whyThisMatters: It applies a known rule of inheritance law to a real case: an heir who improves undivided property cannot keep the gain for himself.

phrases.english: He said to him: He is speaking correctly to you,
phrases.notes: This is רב חסדא speaking to מרי.

phrases.english: as we learned: If one left older and younger sons,
and the older ones improved the property –
they improved it for the middle.
phrases.notes: Meaning the added value goes into the shared pot and is split among all the brothers.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: שַׁפִּיר קָאָמַר לָךְ, דִּתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rules on the claim of Step 22 and supports it with a משנה.
steps.raayaObject: The brother's claim to a share of the orchards and gardens מרי planted.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in בבא בתרא: improvements by older sons to the estate are shared with the younger sons.
